=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Package

**Scope note:** The Seller's efficiency note asks us to review only [OPEN] items and skip [STANDARD] ones. I've reviewed all 16 items, because several [STANDARD] labels cover positions that are adverse to the Buyer. The "FINAL" and "settled at principal level" labels are the Seller's characterisation and don't bind Wattlebridge unless the Buyer has agreed them. Treat all positions as open.

**Top priorities:** Riverlark and the AUD 420k bonuses are price items, not drafting points. Bluefen needs to be a true condition precedent. The privacy incident and the Ironquay IP exposure need specific indemnities. The general regime must not be allowed to absorb the fundamental, tax and IP claims.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** AUD 4.8m (20% of price) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A cap of 20–30% for general warranties only. Fundamental, tax and specific indemnities sit outside it, and known issues are handled by price or specific indemnity, not the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 20% as an opening position for general warranties only. Reason: the cap is within market range, but it must not limit the known exposures.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis per claim, and a AUD 250k deductible basket (only the excess is recoverable), about 1% of price.
- **Buyer should want:** A tipping basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%) and a de minimis of about AUD 10k. Once the basket is exceeded, recovery should be from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket. Reason: a deductible of AUD 250k means the Buyer bears the first AUD 250k of general warranty losses.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, applied to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties, given the open privacy investigation and the Bluefen and Ironquay issues. Longer periods for fundamental, tax and IP claims (see 004 and 016).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months. Reason: 18 months may expire before the privacy and IP issues have been investigated or resolved.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, outside the basket, with a six-year limitation period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: title defects are fundamental to what the Buyer is paying for and should not be limited to a general warranty regime.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** The package is silent on fraud. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations and exclusive remedy to "all Claims of any nature", which would arguably include fraud.
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out for fraud and wilful concealment from all caps, baskets, time limits, disclosure, the knowledge qualifier and the exclusive-remedy clause.
- **Recommendation:** Insert an express carve-out. Reason: courts may be reluctant to enforce a contractual exclusion of a party's own fraud, but an express carve-out avoids argument about it.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Clause 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room as at 22 September 2026. Clause 1.2 adds the accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, fairly disclosed. No general data room disclosure. No disclosure of matters that appear in public registers unless specifically referred to.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Reason: a blanket data room disclosure would effectively remove most warranty protection, since the Buyer cannot read every document against every warranty.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim in respect of anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** A pro-sandbagging clause. Buyer rights are not affected by its knowledge. The Buyer's knowledge of the DD-002 to DD-012 issues must not defeat claims on specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert a pro-sandbagging clause. Reason: the Australian position on sandbagging is not settled, so the protection needs to be express. Clause 8.3 would otherwise defeat claims about issues the Buyer has already identified.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent. Treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). Consent under clause 11.2 has not been obtained, and the conditions in 11.3 are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Consent as an express condition precedent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with no adverse variation. The Buyer alone can waive it. A long-stop date with a termination right. A specific indemnity or price adjustment if the Bluefen revenue is lost after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Make consent a condition precedent and reject "reasonable endeavours" as the sole standard. Reason: a loss of roughly 30% of revenue is a value-critical item and should not depend on endeavours.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release "following Completion". The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Payout at Completion, with a payoff letter and release of all security (including any charge over the shares) delivered at Completion. The payout comes out of the price under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Reason: a debt-free/cash-free price cannot pass with AUD 3.2m of debt left outstanding, and a release after Completion leaves the Buyer exposed to the security.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. DD-005 doesn't say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses, with all on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and other employment costs), treated as debt-like items deducted from the price or paid by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: the bonuses relate to pre-Completion service and transaction completion and under a debt-free/cash-free price belong to the Seller.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW 3 payment. The AUD 180k is open under DD-010, the transfer of SOW 3 Project Materials is conditional on payment under DD-004 clause 7.3, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of the AUD 180k before Completion, or deduction from price. A confirmatory assignment of all SOW 3 Project Materials. A specific indemnity for all Ironquay claims (not just the SOW 3 fee), outside the cap and basket. An IP ownership warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as drafted. Reason: the indemnity does not cover ownership of the IP, which is the real exposure, and the transfer is not yet effective.

**SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident**
- **Seller:** Described as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". No loss amount. DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external address, with about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- **Buyer should want:** A forensic investigation before signing or as a condition precedent. Confirmation of whether an eligible data breach has occurred and whether notification is required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). A specific privacy indemnity outside the cap and basket, possibly backed by an escrow or retention. A privacy and data protection warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not expected to be material" characterisation. Reason: the disclosure itself says the facts are unresolved, and the Buyer cannot price a risk the Seller has not quantified. Confirm the Privacy Act analysis with NSW/Commonwealth privacy counsel.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k, described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Contract review to confirm the renewal terms, whether any run beyond Completion, and whether any are unavoidable or accrued. Any non-ordinary-course commitment to be treated as debt-like or borne by the Seller. An interim covenant requiring Buyer consent before new or renewed supplier commitments above a threshold.
- **Recommendation:** Accept only once contracts are reviewed and the ordinary-course characterisation is confirmed. Reason: DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together, and the disclosure doesn't confirm the characterisation.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all claims. This includes title, tax and IP.
- **Buyer should want:** Four separate regimes: (a) general warranties, with the cap, basket and 24-month limit; (b) fundamental warranties, capped at price, outside the basket, six years; (c) tax, outside the cap and basket, running until 60 days after the statute of limitations expires; (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, Bluefen, privacy incident, bonuses), outside the general regime and not subject to the knowledge qualifier.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: a single regime would expose the Buyer's most serious risks to the general cap, basket and time limit.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%. The disclosure notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** An ASIC company search, a PPSR search over the shares (to check for security interests, including any Riverlark security), inspection of the original share certificates, a statutory declaration from the Seller, and confirmation that no transfer restrictions apply.
- **Recommendation:** Complete these checks before signing. Reason: the register alone is only the Seller's own evidence of title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are said to be "settled under the general regime". No specific tax or IP warranty terms are provided.
- **Buyer should want:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the cap and basket, with a statute-based time limit. Full IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and open-source use, with a longer limit (at least six years). Tax and IP warranties provided in draft for review.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: the Buyer cannot accept a "settled" position for tax and IP when neither set of warranties has been provided.

---

**Other items to resolve:**
- **Bring-down:** The disclosure is as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure and a Seller confirmation that nothing has changed.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent or notice is needed for the share sale.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Confirm the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale.
- **Disclosure letter clause 1.4:** Its "no admission" language is acceptable only if the Seller agrees the disclosed facts can be relied on as stated for the Buyer's risk assessment.

This is an analysis for the deal team, not formal legal advice. The privacy, employment and tax points in particular should be confirmed by NSW counsel and tax advisers before the mark-up goes to the Seller.
